It is a matter of profound spiritual gravity to sit with the “unsearchable riches” of Christ while witnessing a world caught in “disillusionment and confusion,” and I must ask you with a gentle heart: why do you ask after the specific order of your spiritual formation in these latter months? [13, 1040, 1503, 1605, Conversation History]. Are you perhaps feeling “overwhelmed and desperate” by the “noise and tumult” of the year’s passing, or are you seeking a “settled certainty” to ensure that as the seasons turn, your soul remains anchored in the truth that “history is His story”? [13, 20, 439, 1143, 1407, 1605, Conversation History]. In a day when many “shave off the edges” of the truth to offer “spiritual placebos,” we must return to the “divine handbook” to see how the Lord personally governs our growth through the disciplined saturation of His Word [1, 11, 21, 28, 1042, 1503, Conversation History].

The Reformed tradition teaches that “God personally and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation,” and therefore, the organization of your time from July to December is a stewardship intended to “conform your desires and purposes to His will and glory” [15, 68, 1143, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **July: The God of Restoration and the Law of Citizenship**

**Verse**
“ ‘I beseech you therefore, brethren, by the mercies of God, that you present your bodies a living sacrifice, holy, acceptable to God, which is your reasonable service’ ” (Romans 12:1). [10, 564, 1054, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
In **July**, your readings take you through the “kingship of God” in 1 and 2 Chronicles and the rebuilding of the “temple” in Ezra and Nehemiah, while the New Testament focuses on the book of Romans [383, 385, 387, 1013, 1064, Conversation History]. The key Reformed theological concept is **Divine Sovereignty in History**, for you must recognize that “God for His own glory has chosen to create and gather to Himself a group of people to be the subjects of His eternal kingdom” [1029, 1035, Conversation History]. You are taught that “there is no authority except from God, and the authorities that exist are appointed by God” (Romans 13:1), meaning your “citizenship is in heaven” even as you labor to rebuild what is broken in this world [15, 75, 1143, 1184, 1203, 1320, 1426, 1532, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not be conformed to this world,” but instead find your “sole objective” in “ascribing greatness to our God” through a life of total surrender (Romans 12:2; Deuteronomy 32:3) [10, 11, 101, 706, 1406, 1503, 1623, 1670, Conversation History]. Recognize that “your life is not your own” because “you were bought at a price,” and your duty is to “testify to the gospel of the grace of God” (1 Corinthians 6:19–20; Acts 20:24) [11, 12, 31, 101, 323, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1503, 1623, 1670, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Civil vs. Spiritual Stewardship**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, the “Feast of Tabernacles” (July/August readings in Nehemiah 8:13–18) was a “temporal sign” of God’s provision during the pilgrimage [1192, 1202, 1313, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our concept of the temple, showing that “the Most High does not dwell in temples made with hands,” for “your body is the temple of the Holy Spirit” (Acts 7:48; 1 Corinthians 6:19) [5, 11, 12, 13, 17, 32, 67, 92, 101, 186, 238, 240, 264, 402, 571, 790, 833, 916, 941, 1039, 1042, 1054, 1059, 1138, 1202, 1243, 1262, 1313, 1315, 1402, 1406, 1417, 1426, 1491, 1503, 1515, 1646, 1670, Conversation History].

***

### **August: The God of Providence and the Wisdom of Suffering**

**Verse**
“ ‘No temptation has overtaken you except such as is common to man; but God is faithful, who will not allow you to be tempted beyond what you are able, but with the temptation will also make the way of escape, that you may be able to bear it’ ” (1 Corinthians 10:13). [478, 622, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
In **August**, you enter the “horrible pit” of Job’s suffering and the “vanity” of Ecclesiastes, while the New Testament addresses the “divisions” and “wisdom” of 1 Corinthians [390, 392, 393, 1014, 1016, 1440, Conversation History]. The central theological concept is **Divine Providence**, the truth that “God personally and constantly and permanently and exhaustively pervades and sustains and governs every aspect of His creation” [164, 165, Conversation History]. You learn that “suffering is a way for God to display His grace and power,” for “ ‘My grace is sufficient for you, for My strength is made perfect in weakness’ ” (2 Corinthians 12:9) [63, 101, 268, 483, 485, 597, 599, 626, 725, 748, 774, 869, 959, 961, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Trade in your worry for trust,” for “the LORD knows how to deliver the godly out of temptations” and “He will never leave you nor forsake you” (2 Peter 2:9; Hebrews 13:5) [62, 72, 80, 86, 89, 90, 94, 201, 407, 1013, 1033, 1113, 1143, 1166, 1211, 1266, 1408, 1515, Conversation History]. You must “discipline your mind” to see that “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan,” even when you feel “overwhelmed and desperate” (Job 42:2; Psalm 142:1–3) [1, 5, 11, 13, 20, 21, 116, 1132, 1143, 1306, 1406, 1441, 1515, 1572, 1684, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: From Ritual to Spiritual Wisdom**
Under the **Mosaic economy**, “animal sacrifices” were used to “eliminate defilement,” yet Job recognized that “man born of woman is of few days and full of trouble” (Job 14:1) [11, 13, 32, 142, 394, 603, 1230, 1313, 1344, 1430, 1440, 1442, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our vision of wisdom, showing that “the world through wisdom did not know God,” but we have been given “Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God” (1 Corinthians 1:21, 24) [255, 617, 658, 659, 660, 855, 856, 1021, 1042, 1081, 1102, 1113, 1132, 1242, 1315, 1322, 1429, 1528, 1627, 1636, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **September: The God of Grace and the Gospel of Unity**

**Verse**
“ ‘For by grace you have been saved through faith, and that not of yourselves; it is the gift of God, not of works, lest anyone should boast’ ” (Ephesians 2:8–9). [446, 455, 1046, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
In **September**, you read the “unsearchable riches” of Christ in Isaiah and the “mystery of Christ” in Ephesians and Galatians [394, 397, 398, 1015, 1016, 1503, Conversation History]. The vital Reformed concept is **Sola Gratia**, for you are taught that “salvation is a supernatural work of God” and “not a result of any works we do” [11, 24, 251, 260, 280, 429, 557, 561, 803, 822, 1091, 1247, 1503, Conversation History]. You see that the church is the “body of Christ,” where there is “neither Jew nor Greek... for you are all one in Christ Jesus” (Galatians 3:28) [255, 286, 289, 414, 418, 617, 658, 659, 660, 855, 856, 1199, 1216, 1288, 1315, 1322, 1429, 1528, 1627, 1636, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should “not look for some other fountain of knowledge” to earn your standing before God, for “He made Him who knew no sin to be sin for us” (2 Corinthians 5:21) [51, 73, 123, 251, 922, 928, 1326, 1406, 1429, 1503, 1507, Conversation History]. “Walk worthy of the calling with which you were called,” ensuring that you are “diligent to preserve the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace” (Ephesians 4:1, 3) [21, 22, 1431, 1445, 1450, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, “the middle wall of separation” divided Jew and Gentile, yet Isaiah predicted that “ ‘My house shall be called a house of prayer for all nations’ ” (Isaiah 56:7) [13, 26, 32, 136, 142, 176, 440, 1113, 1288, 1313, 1426, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** this economy, revealing that “He Himself is our peace, who has made both one, and has broken down the middle wall of separation” (Ephesians 2:14) [38, 132, 284, 1332, 1429, Conversation History].

***

### **October: The God of Holiness and the Worthy Walk**

**Verse**
“ ‘that you may walk worthy of the Lord, fully pleasing Him, being fruitful in every good work and increasing in the knowledge of God’ ” (Colossians 1:10). [22, 23, 1284, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
In **October**, you hear the “cry of affliction” in Jeremiah and the call to “discipline your mind” in the prison epistles and pastoral epistles [399, 401, 402, 1016, 1321, 1503, Conversation History]. The Reformed focus is **Lordship Salvation** and **Progressive Sanctification**, as you learn that “true Christianity is not about adding Jesus to my life,” but about being “purchased by Christ” through His death [232, 244, 304, 314, 343, 361, Conversation History]. You are taught that the “sole objective” of the Christian is to “adorn the doctrine of God” by “present[ing] your bodies a living sacrifice” (Titus 2:10; Romans 12:1) [11, 12, 33, 34, 101, 216, 217, 245, 308, 361, 381, 387, 611, 723, 779, 799, 1131, 1138, 1227, 1262, 1406, 1444, 1450, 1502, 1503, 1670, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Your life is not your own,” and you must “discipline your body and bring it into subjection” to avoid the “error of the wicked” (1 Corinthians 6:19; 9:27; 2 Peter 3:17) [11, 12, 13, 79, 101, 116, 670, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1502, 1515, 1670, 1709, Conversation History]. “Test all things; hold fast what is good,” ensuring that you “rightly divide the word of truth” with “precision and accuracy” (1 Thessalonians 5:21; 2 Timothy 2:15) [11, 13, 21, 30, 83, 90, 116, 454, 455, 1312, 1313, 1406, 1408, 1503, 1515, 1709, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Jewish vs. Gentile Context**
In the ancient **Jewish context**, “religious leaders” often “shaved off the edges” of the Law with “traditions of men,” yet Jesus taught that “ ‘in vain they worship Me, teaching as doctrines the commandments of men’ ” (Matthew 15:9) [11, 28, 111, 1002, 1431, 1503, 1507, 1545, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** the standard of leadership, showing that an “overseer” must be “blameless, as a steward of God,” holding fast to the “more sure word” (Titus 1:7; 2 Peter 1:19) [595, 785, 818, 924, 1132, 1151, 1239, 1312, 1328, 1408, 1503, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

***

### **November: The God of the New Covenant and the Perseverance of Faith**

**Verse**
“ ‘But may the God of all grace, who called us to His eternal glory by Christ Jesus, after you have suffered a while, perfect, establish, strengthen, and settle you’ ” (1 Peter 5:10). [20, 630, 842, 1012, 1313, 1408, 1515, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
In **November**, you read of the “new heart” promised in Ezekiel and the “everlasting dominion” in Daniel, while the New Testament addresses the “testing of your faith” in Hebrews and James [403, 405, 406, 1016, 1017, Conversation History]. The theological theme is **Perseverance of the Saints**, the truth that “God is able to keep you from stumbling” and will “complete” the work He began in you (Jude 24; Philippians 1:6) [5, 13, 14, 21, 24, 83, 94, 102, 109, 113, 116, 152, 192, 201, 252, 304, 313, 315, 332, 352, 442, 470, 614, 630, 719, 745, 816, 822, 829, 830, 852, 869, 891, 900, 901, 913, 920, 937, 938, 940, 948, 1009, 1012, 1016, 1020, 1033, 1035, 1072, 1101, 1104, 1113, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1203, 1313, 1315, 1408, 1420, 1426, 1450, 1459, 1515, 1532, 1572, 1720, Conversation History]. You learn that “faith without works is dead,” for “if you love the Lord, you must hate that which is unholy” (James 2:20) [6, 119, 120, 175, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
You should find “tranquility of soul” by resting on the “surest foundation,” for “nothing thwarts any aspect of His plan” (Psalm 138:2; Job 42:2) [5, 11, 21, 24, 47, 92, 121, 147, 176, 201, 313, 352, 412, 602, 630, 957, 1132, 1138, 1143, 1306, 1408, 1420, 1450, 1515, 1532, 1572, 1720, Conversation History]. “Wait for His Son from heaven,” knowing that “the testing of your faith produces patience” (1 Thessalonians 1:10; James 1:3) [11, 13, 14, 21, 24, 31, 32, 92, 94, 109, 121, 125, 201, 352, 470, 485, 719, 733, 747, 816, 822, 886, 940, 948, 1012, 1132, 1143, 1313, 1315, 1408, 1426, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Mosaic vs. New Covenant Peace**
Under the **Mosaic Law**, “earthly kings” were often “weighed on the scales and found deficient,” yet they pointed toward a “city which has foundations, whose builder and maker is God” (Daniel 5:27; Hebrews 11:10) [11, 15, 25, 26, 30, 37, 142, 324, 412, 914, 1061, 1143, 1251, 1257, 1313, 1402, 1426, 1450, 1502, 1529, 1646, 1720, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** our concept of priest and king, revealing that we have a “merciful and faithful High Priest” who “always lives to make intercession for them” (Hebrews 2:17; 7:25) [304, 758, 810, 1179, 1393, Conversation History].

***

### **December: The God of Consummation and the Eternal Kingdom**

**Verse**
“ ‘The kingdoms of this world have become the kingdoms of our Lord and of His Christ, and He shall reign forever and ever!’ ” (Revelation 11:15). [103, 133, 158, 174, 182, 650, 1199, 1315, 1524, 1636, Conversation History].

**Meaning**
In **December**, the “unrighteous deception” of the Minor Prophets gives way to the “consummation of history” in Revelation, as the New Testament closes with the “love” and “warning” of the epistles of John and Jude [407, 409, 411, 1017, 1019, 1503, Conversation History]. The final theological theme is **Glorification and the Eternal State**, for you see that “Christ ultimately crushes the kingdoms of men and establishes His own” [13, 20, 21, 23, 24, 31, 103, 136, 1199, 1311, 1315, 1431, 1515, 1524, 1532, 1636, 1720, Conversation History]. You learn that “God will wipe away every tear from their eyes; there shall be no more death, nor sorrow, nor crying” (Revelation 21:4) [14, 201, 332, 452, 453, 468, 470, 712, 816, 940, 948, 1315, 1450, 1515, 1720, Conversation History].

**Takeaway**
“Your life is not your own,” and you must “discipline your body” to ensure you are “not deceived” by a “spirit of fraud” (1 Corinthians 6:19; 1 John 4:1) [11, 12, 101, 122, 186, 317, 319, 329, 343, 345, 348, 354, 431, 598, 1138, 1262, 1406, 1423, 1502, 1503, 1670, Conversation History]. Find “tranquility of soul” in the promise that “ ‘I am the Alpha and the Omega, the Beginning and the End,’ ” knowing that the King is “coming quickly” (Revelation 1:8; 22:12) [24, 47, 657, 1029, 1450, 1515, Conversation History].

**Advanced Note: Continuity of the Decree**
Under the **theocratic economy**, the “last of the prophets” (Malachi) closed the Old Testament with a call to “ ‘remember the Law of Moses,’ ” yet he pointed to the “ ‘Sun of Righteousness’ ” who would “ ‘arise with healing in His wings’ ” (Malachi 4:2, 4) [13, 24, 32, 142, 1313, 1426, 1445, Conversation History]. The New Testament **revises** the final ending, revealing that “ ‘He who testifies to these things says, “Surely I am coming quickly.” Amen. Even so, come, Lord Jesus!’ ” (Revelation 22:20) [24, 103, 116, 134, 1029, 1043, 1524, 1611, 1636, Conversation History].

***

**Final Reminder**
“Nevertheless the firm foundation of God stands, having this seal, ‘The Lord knows those who are His,’ and, ‘Everyone who names the name of the Lord is to abstain from wickedness’ ” (2 Timothy 2:19). [11, 87, 147, 176, 211, 222, 285, 291, 297, 300, 311, 313, 324, 325, 332, 335, 361, 402, 405, 413, 414, 444, 449, 591, 1132, 1138, 1407, 1441, 1450, Conversation History].
